findings.title: Substring check for event.type:error also matches negated and mixed queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query contains the substring `event.type:error`. That includes negated queries such as `!event.type:error` and mixed ones such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For these the discover dataset will swap `count()` for `sum(sample_weight)`. Transactions have no sample_weight, so counts come out wrong, and a negated query counts the opposite set of events with the wrong aggregation. The check should parse the query, or at least reject negation and OR'd transaction filters.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but passes the closed-over request `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-split path, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover`, using an errors-only query (`!event.type:transaction`), while the outer dataset is metrics_enhanced_performance. The decision is then made against the wrong dataset, so error counts in the split path are never upsampled. The reverse mismatch is also possible. The check should use `scoped_dataset` and the actual query being executed rather than `request.GET['query']`.

findings.title: Cache key built from hash() of project ids can collide; invalidation is ineffective
findings.body:
The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))` instead of the ids themselves. Distinct project sets can collide on this hash, and a colliding request would get another project set's eligibility result. Projects that are not allowlisted could then be upsampled, or the reverse.

The cache is also keyed by org, while the allowlist is a global option. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called and can only clear one exact project set, so it cannot keep the cache consistent when the option changes.

The cache also adds a network roundtrip in front of `options.get`, which is already cached in-process. The claimed performance gain is doubtful, and the cache adds up to 60s of staleness.

findings.title: Docstring claims fresh reads, contradicting the caching layer
findings.body: The NOTE says `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` reads the allowlist fresh each time to always reflect the latest configuration. Its only caller wraps it in a 60-second cache, so the note is misleading. The `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` docstring also describes `sum(sample_weight)` while the code emits `upsampled_count()`.

findings.title: upsampled_count silently undercounts events without sample_weight
findings.body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` assumes every event has a populated sample_weight. Events ingested before sampling was enabled, or sent without client sampling context, will have null or zero weight. Those events contribute nothing, so counts drop instead of falling back to 1 per event. A safer expression is `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` or similar.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink/submodule committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink that points at the base commit. There is no matching .gitmodules entry and it is unrelated to the feature. It looks like a local checkout committed by mistake, and it will break clones and tooling that process submodules. Remove it.

findings.title: No tests for the cached entrypoint or negated queries
findings.body: The tests cover the private helpers but never call `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. Its caching behaviour, including stale results when the option changes, is untested. `_is_error_focused_query` is not tested with `!event.type:error` or OR'd queries, which hides the substring-match bug. `self.snuba_params` is built in setUp but never used.
